case_source: Re-numbered as Civil Revision No. 4793 of 1991 (Dhaka)
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Nuruzzaman, J :- The instant Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show-cause as to why' the impugned Judgment and Decree complained of in the petition moved in Court shall not be set aside.

2. The material facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, is that the predecessor of the plaintiff-opposite party Nos.1-11 Abdul Karim instituted Title Suit No.137 of 1976 in the Court of learned Munsif, 3rd Court, Sadar, Jessore against the defendants for declaration of title and confirmation of possession over the suit land. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that the "Ka" schedule land originally belonged to one Ayezuddin Biswas and during his possession he settled the suit land to Abdul Karim, the predecessor of the plaintiff-opposite parties by way of registered Kabuliyat dated 05.3.1937. The "Kha" schedule land belonged to Chandra Bibi and she settled the suit land to Abdul Karim by way of Kabuliyat dated 24.6.1950 at a rental of Rs.5/5/- Annas. Since the date of settlement the plaintiffs had been owning and possessing the suit land. But -/8/- Annas share of the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of the defendants which is wrong and fraudulent. The defendants have got no right, title and interest and possession in the suit land. The cause of action to file the suit arose on 27th of Chaitra, 1387 B.S. when the defendants denied the plaintiff's title and threaten to dispossess from the suit land. Hence, the plaintiff was compelled to file the instant suit.

3. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint. The defendant's case, in short, is that the "Ka" schedule land originally belonged to Herajatullah and Derajatullah under the landlord of Motinessa and others and the "Kha" schedule land also belonged to Heraj and Deraj in equal share under the landlord Roton Bibi and during their possession C.S. record of rights correctly published their name. Deraj died leaving his daughter Hajari and brother Heraj. Heraj died leaving two sons namely Abdul Karim, the deceased plaintiff and Abdul Jalil, the predecessor of the defendants. The share of Heraj was devolved upon both Abdul Karim and Abdul Jalil equally. Abdul Karim instituted the suit. Thereafter, Abdul Karim died leaving one widow, 5 sons and 5 daughters and Abdul Jalil died leaving this defendants. This contesting defendants inherited -/8/-Annas share in the suit land through their father. The -/8/- Annas share of the suit land has rightly been recorded in the name of this defendants. The defendants have been owning and possessing their share land. The father of the plaintiff never acquired the suit land alone. The plaintiff did not possess -/16/- Annas share, rather they possess their -/8/- Annas share in the suit land. Hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.

4. The trial Court after perusing the pleadings of the respective parties framed as many as 5 issues which are as follows :

(I) Is the suit maintainable in its present form ?

(II) Is the suit barred by limitation ?

(III) Is the suit properly valued and duly stamped ?

(IV) Have the plaintiff any right, title, interest and possession in the suit land ?

(V) To what relief, if any, the plaintiff are entitled ?

5. At the trial both the parties led their respective evidence to prove their case. The plaintiff examined as many as 4 P.Ws. and the defendants also examined 4 D.Ws. The trial Court after considering the materials on record dismissed the suit.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 28th March, 1980 passed by the learned Munsif, 3rd Court, Jessore the plaintiff as appellant preferred Title Appeal No.88 of 1980 before the learned District Judge, Jessore and eventually the Title Appeal was transferred to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge, Jessore who by his judgment and decree dated 14.6.1982 and 21.6.1982 respectively allowed the appeal reversing those dated 28.3.1980 passed by the learned Munsif, 3rd Court, Sardar, Jessore.

7. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 14.6.1982 and 21.6.1982 respectively the defendant-respondent as petitioner preferred the instant revisional application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule with an order of stay.

8. Mr. M.A. Wahab, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Court of appeal below committed an error of law apparent on the face of the records by observing that "it cannot be concluded that the title and interest of the land remained with the recorded persons simply because the land was recorded in their names at the time of C.S. operation" which is a clear violation of the provision of Section 103 B(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act. He further added that the appellate Court below committed an error of law in holding that "the Kabuliyat Ext.2 and 2(a) sufficiently proved that Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi acquired interest in the "Ka" and "Kha" schedule lands respectively" in view of the fact that there is no iota of evidence either in the plaint or in the deposition of the witnesses of the plaintiffs that Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi ever acquired the disputed land from the admitted recorded tenants Derajtullah Biswas and Herajtulalh Biswas rather it is on the record that the "Ka" schedule land originally belonged to Satkori Mitra and Hemlal Mitra which is all together a wrong,false and baseless in view of the Exts.3(d) and 3(e). He further submitted that the Court of appeal below committee an error of law by giving importance and reliance upon the Kabuliyat Exts.2 and 2(a) which have not been legally and properly proved by the plaintiff in this case. He further submitted that the appellate Court committed an error of law in holding that "Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi acquired interest in the land of C.S Khatian No.47 and C.S Khatian No.207," in fact that there is no evidence to that effect that both of them took settlement of the said "Ka" and "Kha" schedule lands respectively from the original owner. He added that the appellate Court also committed an error of law in placing reliance upon the S.A. record in respect of the non-disputed land. He further submitted that the appellate Court committed an error of law by misreading the deposition of witnesses, particularly the deposition of the D.Ws. 2 and 3. He further submitted that the appellate Court also committed an error of law in not considering the evidence of P.W.1 Abdus Salam who has admitted the possession of the defendant No.1 in the disputed Plot Nos.50 and 52 by deposing that the distance between the homestead of the plaintiffs and the defendants No.1 Soleman is one bighat only, where in the defendant No.1 has admittedly been resided with his family in his ancestral homestead situated in the same Plot. In such view of the evidence the appellate Court erred in law in not holding that the defendants are in possession of the suit land. He further submitted that the appellate Court committed an error of law in placing importance and relying upon the Dhakilas Ext.1-series which have not been proved in accordance with law and the procedure. He further submitted that Ext.1 series are not genuine, rather forged, fraudulent and created for the purpose of the suit. But the appellate Court below committed an error of law on relying upon the Dhakilas Ext.1- series and as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He also submitted that the appellate Court committed an error of law. in not considering the petition filed by the respondent No.1 stating that the respondent No.2 died on 7.10.1980 and the appeal was abated as the heir/heirs of respondent No.2 Chandra Bibi was not made party in time. He added that the plaintiffs must prove his own case and weaknesses of the defence case, the plaintiff will not be entitled to get any benefit. According to him the' plaintiff failed to prove the case resulting which the trial Court dismissed the suit. But the appellate Court below without controverting the findings of the trial Court on misreading the evidence, misconstrued the documents, thus, mere surmise and conjecture allowed the appeal. He also referred the evidence of D.Ws. and submitted that from which it is apparent that the appellate court committed error of law, and as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside.

9. None appears to oppose the Rule.

<u>10. Having gone though the impugned judgment it appears that the appellate Court opined "that the plaintiffs have produced certified copy of the Kabuliyat dated 05.2.1937 Ext.2 and the certified copy of the Kabuliyat dated 24.6.1950 Ext.2(a) to show that Ayejudiin Biswas acquired C.S. Plot Nos.50 and 52 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.47 and Chandra Bibi became owner of the entire land of C.S. Khatian No.207. The Kabuliyat Ext.2 was executed about 45 years back and Kabuliyat Ext.2(a) was executed more than 30 years back, so in my opinion that those old documents should be given due importance. It has been argued on behalf of the defendant-respondent that the plaintiff could not produce any document to show as to how Ayejudiin Biswas and Chandra Bibi acquired their interest in the suit Plots. It is true that the plaintiffs have not produced any documents regarding the title of Ayejuddin Biswas in "Ka" schedule land and Chandra Bibi in respect of "Kha" schedule land. I think the Kabuliyat Ext.2 and 2(a) sufficiently proved that Ayejuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi acquired interest in the "Ka" and "Kha" schedule land respectively. If Ayejuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi had no interest in the said property, there was no reason why Abdul Karim (since dead) would execute Kabuliyat in their favour." After appreciating the materials on record I am of the view that the above findings neither correct nor based on material evidence on record. Further this court is of the view that while C.S. record of rights admittedly stands in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiff and defendants by executing Kabuliyat one of them i.e. by plaintiff, surely no right, title will create by such Kabuliyat either in favour of Kabuliyat giver and receiver. Kabuliyat receiver, or giver must proved that he had right, title and interest over suit property. In the instant case although Kabuliyat receiver was examined by the plaintiff as P.W. but he failed to produce any documentary evidence in his favour showing that he was the real owner of the suit khatian by any documentary evidence in other capacity, and as such, far away to admit the alleged Kabuliyat as his title. I am of the view that a unilateral Kabuliyat does not confer the title either parties without basis of proof of any documentary evidence.</u>

<u>11. On perusal of the impugned judgment it appears that the appellate Court itself has made a query in its judgment regarding title of the suit property while plaintiff Abdul Karim executed Kabuliyat in favour of Ayezuddin Biswas from which it further manifest that the court of appeal below was in doubt about the title of the Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi.</u>

<u>12. On the other hand from the judgment of the trial Court it appears that the trial court opined that the defendant claimed ejmali possession and he claimed his title on the basis of heir of C.S. recorded tenant Herajtullah. Both the C.S. and S.A. porcha go to protect the right and title of defendant. It is the case of the defendant that the Kabuliyat, i.e., Exts.2 and 2(a) have been created for the purpose of case and those are forged and concocted documents. The appellate Court did not consider the legal aspect of the Exts.2 and 2(a) because according to the trial Court these 2 exhibits neither proved the title of the receiver and giver nor produced and proved in accordance with law. In my opinion Exts.2 and 2(a) since produced by the plaintiff it is the onus of the plaintiff to prove the same in accordance with law but in the trial Court they have failed to prove these exhibits complying with the relevant provision of law. Moreover, one of the admitted owner if make any Kabuliyat in favour of title less third party admitting right, title and interest who has no such right and title, that unilateral Kabuliyat should not be admitted and accepted as title deed. Furthermore, on perusal of the material on record it appears that all the exhibits produced by the plaintiff received back by the plaintiff-opposite parties, although from this Court once again reminders were issued to produce the wanting exhibit documents before this Court but they failed to do so. Therefore, this court has no scope, chance or occasion to perused and consider the same.</u>

13. The trial Court while dismissed the suit clearly opined that P.W3 claimed to be the son of Chandra Bibi and he deposes that his mother got the suit land by way of auction purchase, but no such paper has been connected or submitted before the any Courts. The trial Court also found that both in C.S. and S.A. Porcha of the suit land were not recorded in the name of Chandra Bibi. Only in S.A. Porcha of Khatian No.269 her name was included in equal share with the name of the father of the plaintiff and defendants.

14. From the depositions of the P.Ws and D.Ws and documentary evidence it clearly proved that father of the defendant was in possession of the suit property at the time of S.A. operation and since then the defendants had been owning and possessing the suit property which apparently admitted by the P.W1 in cross-examination. However, the court of appeal below failed to discuss the evidence in respect of C.S and S.A. record to its legal and true perspective which are the vital and most important documentary evidence in favour of not only defendant but also the plaintiff predecessor. So, it can not be said that the plaintiffs had and the defendant had no title over the suit land.

Apart from those documentary evidence it is further crystal clear from the oral and documentary evidence of the P,Ws that the Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi had no documentary evidence on which basis the title of late Abdul Karim can be conferred in his favour. On the other hand according to the provisions of section 103 B of the Bengal Tenancy. Act, 1885 the record of rights published in the name of tenant shall be conclusive proof of such Publication from which it is proved beyond all reasonable doubts that predecessor of Late Abdul Karim and Late Abdul Jalil were the real owner of the suit Khatian as per C.S. record of rights which never became unworthy by any other documentary evidence. In support of the above view I may profitably refer to the case of Akrab Ali and others Vs. Zahiruddin Kari and others reported in 30 DLR (SC) 81 wherein it was held:

"According to section 103(B)(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act every entry in a record of rights finally published shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to be incorrect."

<u>15. On the above facts, circumstances of the case and discussions made hereinabove I am of the firm view that the learned Additional District Judge did not correctly appreciate and construe the documents and materials on record in accordance with law in reversing the judgment of the trial Court. Therefore, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Jessore suffers from legal infirmity and perversity, and as such, the same is liable to be set aside.</u>

16. Thus, the Rule having merit, it succeeds.

17. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

18. The impugned judgment and decree dated 14.6.1982 and 28.6.1982 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Jessore in Title Appeal No.88 of 1980 are hereby set aside and judgment and decree of the trial Court are hereby restored and confirmed.

19. Send down the lower Court record communicate this judgment at once.

End.
